**What importance means here.** Each entry is a specific mathematical question. Importance considers the significance of a resolution, centrality within its field, reach across fields, scholarly and historical fame, broader recognition, and scientific or practical impact.

**How problems are ranked.** LLMs compare pairs of problems. A reliability-weighted model combines those judgments into the ranking, with calibration across model families. The model-family weights are OpenAI 1.00, Claude 1.00, GLM 0.95, and DeepSeek 0.90. These are modeling choices, not measured probabilities of correctness.

**What a rank means.** Nearby ranks can be uncertain. The expanded entries include available ranking ranges and comparison counts. Filtering or alphabetizing the directory preserves every problem’s rank in this edition.

**Diagnostics from the preceding source fit.** After the reported resolutions, edition ranks were compacted without a new numerical fit. The displayed uncertainty ranges and comparison counts come from the preceding fit of 1,280 targets; the current eligible pool contains 1,122. These diagnostics were not recomputed for the smaller pool.

**Related and nested problems.** A substantial subproblem or generalization may receive its own rank when it has independent mathematical standing. Families identify narrow groups of related questions; an implication alone does not merge their families. The ranking process checks family crowding, including a diagnostic retaining the highest-ranked member of each family. Family membership does not itself change scores, impose a quota, or create an automatic penalty.

**Dates and sources.** The edition date identifies this list. A status review date, when recorded, appears separately inside each entry; it does not promise that the literature has been checked since then. Source links identify the exact formulation and available status evidence.

The ranking preserves a fixed edition. Separately dated status notes cover 176 of 500 entries; this is not a fresh literature review of the whole list. Recent resolution claims and formulation concerns are marked below with their historical ranks retained.

Select a problem to read its exact statement, why it matters, status, sources, and related research.

Families are ordered by their highest-ranked member in the complete edition. Families have no importance score; every problem keeps its edition rank. Filters show matching members within that fixed family order.

2. <small>Rank</small>**002****Riemann Hypothesis**Do all zeros of the Riemann zeta function inside the strip with real part between zero and one lie exactly on its middle line?Number theory & arithmetic geometry[Riemann hypotheses and exceptional zeros · 3 problems](https://www.proofatlas.ai/open-problems/#family-context-problem-riemann-hypothesis) Exact statementFor the meromorphic continuation of the Riemann zeta function zeta(s)=sum_{n>=1} n^(-s), initially defined for Re(s)>1, every zero s in the open critical strip 0<Re(s)<1 has Re(s)=1/2. This is the Riemann Hypothesis for zeta alone; it does not assert simplicity of its zeros. Why it mattersA proof would sharply control fluctuations in the distribution of primes: the prime-counting function would differ from its logarithmic-integral approximation by at most O(√x log x). A disproof would invalidate this equivalent error bound.Status**Open**Earlier note (2026-09-14): Riemann remains open. September 2026 progress on the proportion of simple critical-line zeros is partial, not proof that every nontrivial zero lies on the line. Uncorroborated or inaccessible proof claims were not accepted. October 7, 2026: OpenAI’s October 6 release reports partial progress. A zero-free half-plane Re(s)>7/8 for zeta excludes only the right-hand part of the critical strip. The target requires every nontrivial zero to have real part exactly 1/2; no conclusion excluding zeros between 1/2 and 7/8 is supplied. This is partial zero-location progress, not the Riemann Hypothesis. No independent proof audit or Lean verification was performed for this update.Status reviewed Oct 7, 2026 Sources[Enrico Bombieri, Problems of the Millennium: the Riemann Hypothesis, Section I and the prime-counting equivalence.](https://www.claymath.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/riemann.pdf)<small>Statement source</small>[Riemann Hypothesis](https://www.claymath.org/millennium/riemann-hypothesis/)<small>Status source · Retrieved Sep 14, 2026</small>[A new proof that more than 2/3 of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple and on the critical line](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.02882)<small>Status source · Retrieved Sep 14, 2026</small>[Lamzouri lecture at Max Planck Institute for Mathematics, September 3, 2026](https://math-events.uni-bonn.de/event/1560/)<small>Status source · Retrieved Sep 14, 2026</small>[On the Extended, Generalized, and Grand Riemann Hypotheses: A Unified Approach Based on the General Properties of L-Functions — Weicun Zhang, v19](https://www.preprints.org/manuscript/202506.0481)<small>Status source · Retrieved Sep 14, 2026</small>[OpenAI mathematics release, manuscript family 003 (6 October 2026)](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/The-Quasi-Riemann-Hypothesis-September-30-2026/paper.pdf)<small>Status source · Retrieved Oct 7, 2026</small> Research on ProofAtlas[**Riemann Hypothesis**ProofAtlas research · Research on this exact problem](https://www.proofatlas.ai/collaboration/riemann-hypothesis/) Related problems[#10 · Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions](https://www.proofatlas.ai/open-problems/#problem-the-generalized-riemann-hypothesis-for-dirichlet-l-functions)Stronger assertionGeneralized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functionsA proof of #10 would also establish this assertion. 3. <small>Rank</small>**003****Yang-Mills Existence and Mass Gap**Can a nontrivial Yang–Mills quantum field theory in four-dimensional spacetime be constructed rigorously for every compact simple gauge group—the choice of internal symmetry—with a positive, finite gap between vacuum energy and the remaining energy spectrum?Mathematical physics Exact statementFor every compact simple gauge group G, prove that a nontrivial four-dimensional quantum Yang-Mills theory on R^4 exists with all existence requirements of Jaffe-Witten, Quantum Yang-Mills Theory, sections 3-4, including axiomatic properties at least as strong as their cited references [45,35], the required gauge-invariant local fields and short-distance compatibility specified there. Its vacuum Hamiltonian H has no spectrum in (0,Delta) for some Delta > 0, and the supremum of such Delta is finite. The official reconstruction and existence requirements are retained by reference, not replaced by an unrestricted equivalence of arbitrary Euclidean and Minkowski theories. An isolated first excited eigenstate, confinement and asymptotic completeness are not additional requirements. Why it mattersThe construction would turn the specified four-dimensional quantum gauge-field model into a theory satisfying the required mathematical axioms. Its spectrum would have a positive, finite gap above vacuum energy, without requiring an isolated first excited eigenstate.Status**Open**The Yang–Mills group released its assessment and the October 28 OpenAI Lean submission on November 10, 2026. The group reports a clean rebuild, axiom audit, Comparator checks and human review supporting an existence construction from four-dimensional Wilson lattice theory for compact simple gauge groups, with subsequential infinite-volume limits and reconstructed component theories. It does not certify the full Jaffe–Witten problem: no mass gap is claimed, and uniqueness across volume subsequences and agreement of component theories remain unresolved. The full existence-and-mass-gap target remains open. Earlier three-dimensional outlines, individual gauge-group claims and withdrawn postings also do not establish the full target. 5. <small>Rank</small>**005****Navier-Stokes Existence and Smoothness: Fefferman A**For an incompressible fluid filling three-dimensional space, with any positive viscosity and no external force, does every smooth, rapidly decaying initial velocity give a flow that stays smooth forever, with uniformly bounded total kinetic energy?Analysis & PDE[Incompressible fluid regularity · 2 problems](https://www.proofatlas.ai/open-problems/#family-context-problem-navier-stokes-existence-and-smoothness) Exact statementProve Fefferman statement (A): for every viscosity nu > 0 and every real smooth divergence-free Schwartz vector field u0 on R^3, with force f identically zero, there are real velocity u and pressure p in C-infinity(R^3 x [0,infinity)) satisfying partial_t u + (u dot grad)u = nu Delta u - grad p, div u = 0 and u(x,0) = u0(x). The velocity energy integral over R^3 of |u(x,t)|^2 is bounded above by one finite constant for all t >= 0; that constant may depend on u0 and nu. Schwartz means every spatial derivative decays faster than every inverse polynomial, as in official condition (4). Smoothness includes time zero. The selected domain is whole space, not the torus. Why it mattersThis asks whether the specified three-dimensional viscous-flow equations can evolve every allowed starting flow for unlimited time without developing a singularity, while keeping total kinetic energy bounded.Status**Open**The entry concerns Fefferman A: unforced whole-space Navier–Stokes regularity for smooth rapidly decaying divergence-free data. OpenAI's September claim addresses forced alternatives C/D, not A. This exact target remains open; the broader prize announcement does not establish an accepted proof. November 12, 2026: Hexagon preprint 2611.00143, dated November 6, claims nonuniqueness of unforced Leray–Hopf solutions from compactly supported initial data singular at the origin, in weak L^3 but not L^3. This does not resolve the ranked Fefferman A target, which requires smooth Schwartz initial data and smoothness at time zero. The claim has not been independently proof-audited, formally replayed or confirmed as refereed in this update.Status reviewed Nov 12, 2026 Sources[Charles L. 6. <small>Rank</small>**006****Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture**For an elliptic curve over the rational numbers, its rank counts the independent infinite-order generators of its group of rational points. Does this rank equal the order of vanishing of its L-function at s = 1—the multiplicity of the zero there, taken as zero when the function is nonzero?Number theory & arithmetic geometry[Elliptic curve ranks and congruent numbers · 3 problems](https://www.proofatlas.ai/open-problems/#family-context-problem-birch-and-swinnerton-dyer-conjecture) Exact statementProve or disprove that, for every elliptic curve E over the rational numbers, the rank of the finitely generated abelian group E(Q) of rational points equals the order of vanishing at s = 1 of the associated Hasse–Weil L-function L(E, s). Why it mattersA proof would identify an algebraic measure of the curve’s rational points with an analytic measurement of its L-function. A counterexample would locate a curve where those two measurements differ.Status**Open**Earlier note (2026-09-14): BSD rank equality remains open. The located all-rank working-draft claim lacks independent acceptance; recent uses and special cases do not supply a universal proof. October 7, 2026: OpenAI’s October 6 release reports partial progress. The target is equality of analytic and Mordell-Weil ranks for every E/Q, rather than the full leading-term formula. This family gives that equality and the stronger leading-term conclusion when the full q-power Selmer corank is zero or one for some prime q. It leaves curves outside that hypothesis untreated, so it is a low-corank subcase only. The companion proves rank equality for E/Q with nonzero rational two-torsion and full 2-power Selmer corank zero or one, allowing arbitrary reduction at 2. The BSD rank target includes every E/Q without either restriction, so this is a limited subcase and does not follow as a full closure from the H10 result. The low-corank 2-converse explicitly gives equality of analytic and Mordell-Weil ranks for E/Q whose full 2-power Selmer corank is zero or one. The family also supplies analytic rank densities and their mean over twists, but an average or density-one assertion does not prove rank equality for every curve or every twist. No independent proof audit or Lean verification was performed for this update.Status reviewed Oct 7, 2026 Sources[Clay Mathematics Institute, The Millennium Prize 13. <small>Rank</small>**013****NP versus P/poly**Can every yes-or-no problem with short, efficiently checkable evidence for yes answers be solved by Boolean circuits of polynomial size, if a separate circuit may be chosen for each input length? No efficient method of constructing those circuits is required.Theoretical computer science Exact statementDetermine the truth of NP subseteq P/poly. Here NP consists of languages over finite binary strings accepted by nondeterministic Turing machines in polynomial time. P/poly consists of languages L for which there exist constants C>=1 and integer k>=1 and Boolean circuits C_n for all n>=0, of size at most C(n+1)^k, deciding membership in L on every length-n input. Circuits are finite acyclic single-output circuits with fan-in-two AND/OR, fan-in-one NOT, input bits and hardwired constants0/1; count all nodes. Each language has its own bound and circuit family, with no uniform generation requirement. Why it mattersContainment would collapse the polynomial hierarchy to its second level by the Karp–Lipton theorem. Noncontainment would establish a general circuit-size barrier for an NP language and imply P ≠ NP.Status**Open**NP containment in nonuniform P/poly remains open; February 2026 notes pose the matching general-circuit question. Restricted circuits and Karp–Lipton implications do not decide it.Status reviewed Sep 14, 2026 Sources[Arora and Barak, Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach, web draft January8,2007, Definitions6.1–6.3 and Theorem6.13; Aaronson, P ?= NP, Conjecture25.](https://theory.cs.princeton.edu/complexity/book.pdf)<small>Statement source</small>[Boolean Circuits and P/poly, Cornell CS 6810, February 26, 2026](https://www.cs.cornell.edu/courses/cs6810/2026sp/lec10.pdf)<small>Status source · Retrieved Sep 14, 2026</small> Problem familyNP versus P/poly · 1 problem in this edition. 16. <small>Rank</small>**016****BQP Versus NP: Complete Language-Class Relation**How do efficient quantum solving and efficient classical verification compare for yes-or-no problems? Does quantum computation with bounded error solve every problem with short, efficiently checkable evidence for yes answers—and do all problems it solves have such evidence?Theoretical computer science Exact statementDetermine the truth values of BOTH NP subseteq BQP and BQP subseteq NP for unrelativized, advice-free classes of total languages over {0,1}. NP consists of languages with polynomial-length binary witnesses and a deterministic polynomial-time verifier. BQP consists of languages decided by polynomial-time uniformly generated polynomial-size quantum circuits (a deterministic Turing machine outputs Q_n on 1^n), using Watrous's fixed Toffoli, Hadamard and phase-i gates with |0> ancillas and discarding, followed by a standard-basis output measurement. On every yes input acceptance is at least 2/3, and on every no input it is at most 1/3. No arbitrary real gate constants, advice or oracle are available. Establish equality, either proper containment, or incomparability. Why it mattersResolving both inclusions would determine whether these computational classes coincide, one strictly contains the other, or neither contains the other. Each outcome gives a different relationship between efficient verification and bounded-error quantum computation.Status**Open**Both unrelativized BQP/NP inclusions remain unresolved on the checked evidence. Random-permutation oracle separations do not settle the stated uniform total-language relationship.Status reviewed Sep 14, 2026 Sources[John Watrous, Quantum Computational Complexity, arXiv:0804.3401v1; language questions corroborated by Scott Aaronson lecture notes.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0804.3401v1)<small>Statement source</small>[Complexity Theory, Lecture 25: Quantum Computing (2) — Markus Krötzsch, January 27, 2025](https://iccl.inf.tu-dresden.de/w/images/4/4d/CT2024-Lecture-25-overlay.pdf)<small>Status source · Retrieved Sep 14, 2026</small>[Introduction to Quantum Information Science lecture notes — Scott Aaronson](https://www.scottaaronson.com/qclec.pdf)<small>Status source · Retrieved Sep 14, 2026</small>[Random Permutations in Computational Complexity — Hitchcock, Sekoni and Shafei (November 11, 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.08786)<small>Status source · Retrieved Sep 14, 2026</small> Problem familyBQP Versus NP: Complete Language-Class Relation · 1 problem in this edition. 27. <small>Rank</small>**027****Matrix-Multiplication Exponent Equals Two**Can two n-by-n rational matrices be multiplied exactly, without division, with a number of arithmetic operations arbitrarily close to quadratic: O(n^(2 + ε)) for every positive ε? Each rational arithmetic operation counts as one step, regardless of the number of bits in its operands.Theoretical computer science Exact statementLet R_Q(n) be the tensor rank over Q of the bilinear map multiplying two n by n rational matrices: the least r for which AB is a sum of r products alpha_j(A) beta_j(B) C_j, with rational linear forms alpha_j, beta_j and rational output matrices C_j. Set omega_Q = inf{tau in R : R_Q(n) = O(n^tau)}. Prove omega_Q = 2. Equivalently, for every epsilon > 0, exact multiplication admits division-free arithmetic circuits over Q of size O(n^(2+epsilon)), counting rational additions, subtractions, multiplications and constant scalar operations at unit cost. Circuits need not be uniformly generated and rational coefficient bit lengths are not charged. Constants and thresholds may depend on epsilon. Literal O(n^2) attainment is not required. Why it mattersA proof would allow exact matrix multiplication with arithmetic exponents arbitrarily close to two and carry through applicable algebraic reductions to other computations. The statement measures arithmetic operations; it leaves coefficient bit costs and literal quadratic attainment outside its guarantee.Status**Open**Earlier note (2026-09-14): The exact rational-field matrix multiplication exponent target remains open. The August 2026 claimed exponent below 2.371177 is not exponent 2; complex-field results require field/scope review before transfer to Q. October 7, 2026: OpenAI’s October 6 release reports partial progress. The primary manuscript gives omega<=9/4 over C; the secondary manuscript explicitly gives omega<2.258 over every characteristic-zero field, including the full field Q. The all-field companion supplies a weaker square bound and the rectangular exponent improvement concerns a different shape. These are arithmetic upper-bound improvements but none gives omega_Q=2. In particular the strongest complex-only headline is not silently restated as an explicit rational-field theorem. 42. <small>Rank</small>**042****The Fontaine-Mazur Conjecture on Geometric Galois Representations**A Galois representation records arithmetic symmetries as matrices. Must every irreducible l-adic representation over a number field, unramified outside finitely many places and de Rham at primes above l—a local condition describing behavior expected from geometry—come from a smooth projective variety’s cohomology, allowing subquotients and Tate twists?Number theory & arithmetic geometry Exact statementLet K be a number field and l a prime. 65. <small>Rank</small>**065****Deligne conjecture on coefficient-equivariant critical motivic L-values**For a pure motive over the rationals, do its critical L-values, divided by the predicted periods and powers of 2πi, come from one element of its coefficient number field across every complex embedding? This asks whether geometric periods account for these values, assuming compatible realizations and analytic continuation giving finite values at those integers.Number theory & arithmetic geometry Exact statementFor every pure motive M over Q with coefficients in a number field E, in Deligne's geometric realization formalism (Betti, de Rham and compatible l-adic realizations with comparison, dual, tensor and Tate-twist structures), and every critical integer n, the normalized finite L-value vector L(M,n)/((2*pi*i)^(n*d_sign)*c^sign(M)) lies in the diagonal E inside E tensor C, where sign=(-1)^n and d_sign=dim_E H_B^sign(M). Here H_B^sign is the sign eigenspace of complex conjugation, and c^sign is the determinant of the Betti/de Rham comparison to the corresponding filtration quotient, computed in E-rational bases and defined modulo E-units as in Deligne1.7/2.6. Critical means that L_infinity(sigma,M,s) and L_infinity(sigma,Mdual,1-s) have no pole at s=n for every embedding sigma:E->C (equivalently use Mdual(1) at -s). Use finite, not completed, L-functions with the compatible E-valued local factors of2.2. Analytic continuation giving finite values at the selected critical integer and the source's well-defined compatible realizations/local factors are defining prerequisites, not assertions proved by this period law and not a restriction to cases whose continuation is already known. The simultaneous embedding vector must come from one element of E; unrelated componentwise algebraicity is insufficient. All-zero values are allowed, but mixed zero/nonzero components do not satisfy the diagonal membership. No general nonvanishing or order-of-zero assertion from Deligne2.7 is appended. Why it mattersA proof would relate critical L-values to Betti–de Rham periods compatibly across all coefficient embeddings. The requirement is one shared algebraic element; separate algebraicity of unrelated components would not suffice.Status**Open · subcases solved**Deligne critical values remain open, with solved subcases for the coefficient-equivariant universal motive target. 74. <small>Rank</small>**074****Weight–Monodromy Conjecture**Monodromy organizes a variety’s l-adic cohomology into layers. Let M be the unique increasing monodromy filtration centred at zero: N(M_j) is contained in M_(j-2)(-1), and N^a:gr^M_a(V)->gr^M_(-a)(V)(-a) is an isomorphism for every a>=0. For EVERY integer j and ANY lift Phi of geometric Frobenius of F_q, every eigenvalue alpha on gr^M_j(V) is conjectured to be algebraic and have absolute value q^((i+j)/2) under ALL complex embeddings. This is purity of weight i+j. Defining N on an open inertia subgroup does not replace K or q. Finite-extension proof reductions must change cardinality and Frobenius consistently. Extending l-adic coefficients does not change the target. The equivalent source convention compares zero-centred M_j with W_(i+j); weight-filtration existence is not an added unresolved assertion. No restriction to projective, semistable, geometrically connected or special complete-intersection varieties is imposed. l=p, crystalline, torsion and arbitrary rigid-analytic analogues are not substituted. PSPACE is the union over integers k>=1 of DSPACE(n^k), with asymptotic constant factors allowed and read-only input cells not counted as work space. EXPTIME is the union over integers k>=1 of DTIME(2^(n^k)), with asymptotic constant factors allowed. Machines are total deciders that halt on every input. 94. <small>Rank</small>**094****Strongly Polynomial Linear Programming**Can every rational linear program be solved deterministically using a number of exact arithmetic operations bounded by a polynomial in the numbers of variables and constraints, independently of the coefficient lengths?Theoretical computer science[Strongly polynomial linear programming and simplex methods · 2 problems](https://www.proofatlas.ai/open-problems/#family-context-problem-strongly-polynomial-linear-programming) Exact statementDoes a uniform deterministic algorithm solve every rational LP max c^T x, Ax <= b, x >= 0, returning an exact optimum or correctly reporting infeasibility or unboundedness, with poly(m,n) exact arithmetic operations and comparisons independent of coefficient encoding lengths and polynomial intermediate representation size in the binary input length? Operations on input and intermediate rationals are addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and comparison. For a stored p/q with q positive, size is ceil(log2(abs(p)+1)) + ceil(log2(q+1)); reduction to coprime terms, floor and bit extraction are not free operations. No nonuniform advice or arbitrary real constants are allowed. The displayed form is without loss under strongly polynomial slack-variable and variable-splitting reductions. This is the deterministic formulation; a randomized algorithm alone does not settle it. Also known asTOPP Problem8; Megiddo strongly polynomial LP question; Smale's ninth problem (rational strongly polynomial formulation) Why it mattersLinear programming is central to optimization. A strongly polynomial algorithm would separate its arithmetic complexity from the size of its coefficients, while also keeping intermediate number representations polynomial in the binary input length.Status**Open**The deterministic strongly polynomial problem for rational linear programming remains open. 140. <small>Rank</small>**140****Congruent Number Problem**Exactly which positive integers occur as the area of a right triangle whose three side lengths are rational numbers?Number theory & arithmetic geometry[Elliptic curve ranks and congruent numbers · 3 problems](https://www.proofatlas.ai/open-problems/#family-context-problem-congruent-number-problem) Exact statementDetermine exactly which positive integers are congruent numbers, i.e. areas of right triangles with all three sides rational, equivalently for which squarefree n the elliptic curve y^2 = x^3 - n^2 x has a rational point with y != 0. Why it mattersA complete answer would classify these rational triangles by their integer areas. For squarefree n, it would also determine exactly when y² = x³ − n²x has a rational point with nonzero y.Status**Open · subcases solved**October 7, 2026: OpenAI’s October 6 release reports partial progress. The rank-equality theorem applies in particular to congruent-number curves y^2=x^3-n^2 x when a full q-power Selmer group has corank at most one; it then identifies whether their Mordell-Weil rank is zero or one. There is no unconditional classification of every squarefree n or a guarantee that every congruent-number curve meets the low-corank hypothesis. Congruent-number curves have rational two-torsion, so the companion identifies their actual rank when their full 2-power Selmer corank is zero or one. This does not decide congruence for every squarefree n: higher-corank twists and an exhaustive criterion are not covered. The low-corank 2-converse applies to those quadratic twists of y^2=x^3-x whose full 2-power Selmer corank is zero or one, giving the corresponding actual rank. Analytic densities and a mean over signed squarefree twists do not by themselves classify every individual positive congruent number. 150. <small>Rank</small>**150****Voevodsky's Smash-Nilpotence Conjecture**If an algebraic cycle with rational coefficients has zero intersection number against every complementary cycle, must multiplying copies of it on a product of sufficiently many copies of the variety make it zero modulo rational equivalence, for every smooth projective variety over any field?Number theory & arithmetic geometry Exact statementFor every field k, every smooth projective k-variety X of dimension d, every integer 0<=r<=d, and every class alpha in CH^r(X)_Q (codimension-r cycles modulo rational equivalence with rational coefficients), assume deg(alpha.beta)=0 for every beta in CH^(d-r)(X)_Q. Voevodsky's smash-nilpotence assertion is that there exists an integer N>=1, depending on alpha, for which the N-fold EXTERNAL product alpha times ... times alpha is zero in CH^(Nr)(X^N)_Q, where X^N is the fibre product over k. No algebraic-closure, characteristic-zero or geometric-connectedness hypothesis is imposed; disconnected smooth projective schemes are interpreted on their pure-dimensional components. The reverse implication, smash-nilpotent implies numerically trivial, is known, so this is equality of numerical and smash equivalence for rational cycles. Neither intersection powers on X, composition powers of correspondences, integral coefficients, nor a uniform or computable exponent replaces this assertion. Why it mattersA proof would characterize numerical triviality by actual vanishing after enough external products. The required exponent may depend on the cycle, and the products take place on powers of the variety rather than within the original variety.Status**Open · subcases solved**Status review date not recorded in this edition Sources[Vladimir Voevodsky, A Nilpotence Theorem for Cycles Algebraically Equivalent to Zero, IMRN1995 no.4,187-198; published IAS snapshot,13pages](https://www.math.ias.edu/vladimir/sites/math.ias.edu.vladimir/files/Nilpotence_theorem_published.pdf)<small>Statement source</small> Problem familyVoevodsky's Smash-Nilpotence Conjecture · 1 problem in this edition. Success requires matching achievable and converse exponents, or an equivalent evaluable exact characterization, for all these parameters. 332. <small>Rank</small>**332****Conforti–Cornuéjols Conjecture: Packing Property Implies Max-Flow Min-Cut**Does every finite clutter with the packing property also have the max-flow min-cut property? Both properties use the stated finite-optimum convention, so an infeasible covering program or an unbounded dual is not a counterexample.Combinatorics & discrete geometry Exact statementFor every finite clutter H, prove or disprove that its packing property implies its max-flow min-cut property. Use the following precise linear-programming convention, with M the edge-by-vertex0/1 incidence matrix: the packing property says that min{w^T x:Mx>=1,x>=0}=max{1^T y:M^T y<=w,y>=0} has integral optimal solutions on both sides for every w in {0,1,+infinity}^V for which the optimum is finite. An infinite cost forces that primal coordinate to0 and omits the corresponding dual upper-bound constraint. The MFMC property requires integral optimal solutions on both sides for every finite nonnegative integral w. Equivalently, packing means the covering/edge-packing min-max equality holds for all minors with the usual feasible-case convention. The reverse implication MFMC implies packing is already known.**Scope qualification.** Apply the stated finite-optimum/feasible-case convention to both packing and MFMC. An infeasible covering LP or unbounded dual is not a failure of the required integral optima. In particular, a clutter containing an empty edge does not constitute a counterexample to this canonical conjecture. 375. <small>Rank</small>**375****Erdős Matching Conjecture**Choose k-element subsets of n objects, forbidding s mutually disjoint choices, with n≥ks. The conjecture asserts |F|<=max{binom(ks-1,k), binom(n,k)-binom(n-s+1,k)}. Here binom(a,k)=0 for integers 0<=a<k. For s=1 the family is empty, and k=1 is included as a trivial case. The two terms are attained by all k-subsets of a fixed (ks-1)-set and by all k-subsets meeting a fixed (s-1)-set, respectively. Why it mattersA negative answer would determine the exact largest size of every such family through the larger of the two constructions. 1. <small>Historical rank</small>**022****Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the Rationals**Is there an algorithm that always halts and correctly decides whether any given integer-coefficient polynomial, in any finite number of variables, has a rational solution?Logic, foundations & set theorySource-reported disproved Historical rank #22 in the Oct 6, 2026 edition. This entry is outside the current open ranking. Exact statement covered by this updateThere exists a total algorithm which, given any finite encoding of a multivariate polynomial f in Z[x_1,...,x_n] with arbitrary finite n and integer coefficients, halts and correctly decides whether there is q in Q^n with f(q)=0. Standard computably interconvertible polynomial encodings are equivalent; no uniform running-time complexity bound is part of the assertion. Status update**Source-reported disproved**Resolved (disproved) on the basis of the OpenAI mathematics release of 6 October 2026. 2. <small>Historical rank</small>**029****Unique Games Conjecture**In a graph-labeling game, each edge requires the two labels to match through a one-to-one rule. Is distinguishing games where almost all rules can be satisfied from those where only a tiny fraction can be satisfied NP-hard, however small these two error thresholds are, with a fixed label set chosen for each pair of thresholds?Theoretical computer scienceSource-reported proved Historical rank #29 in the Oct 6, 2026 edition. This entry is outside the current open ranking. Exact statement covered by this updateFor every fixed pair of real constants epsilon, delta > 0 with epsilon + delta < 1, there exists an integer k >= 2, depending only on epsilon and delta, such that the following promise problem is NP-hard under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions. An instance is a finite directed constraint graph G=(V,E) with E nonempty and, for each edge e=(v,w), a permutation pi_e of [k]. For a labeling L:V->[k], an edge is satisfied if pi_e(L(v))=L(w); val(G) is the largest fraction of satisfied edges over all labelings. Distinguish val(G) >= 1-epsilon from val(G) <= delta, with no requirement on instances between these thresholds. The graph is the growing input; epsilon, delta and k are fixed constants. NP-hardness means that every language in NP has such a reduction mapping yes inputs to the first promised set and no inputs to the second. Status update**Source-reported proved**Resolved (proved) on the basis of the OpenAI mathematics release of 6 October 2026. Exact scope reviewed; proofs not independently audited, refereeing not independently confirmed, and Lean artifacts not executed. Family 102: The manuscript asserts deterministic polynomial-time reductions from 3SAT to fixed-alphabet Unique Games with completeness 1-epsilon and soundness delta for every fixed epsilon,delta in (0,1/2). This covers the ranked range epsilon,delta>0, epsilon+delta<1: choose smaller positive parameters below 1/2 and below the requested values, giving stronger completeness and soundness promises. The alphabet remains fixed independently of the graph input. This is the ordinary UGC target, not merely a conditional approximation consequence.Status reviewed Oct 7, 2026 Resolution sources[OpenAI mathematics release, 6 October 2026; source-reported result, proofs not independently audited](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/The-Unique-Games-Theorem-September-23-2026/paper.pdf)Earlier ranking contextA proof would establish this hardness gap and support approximation thresholds obtained through Unique Games reductions. Claims of efficient-algorithm impossibility from NP-hardness would still require the assumption P ≠ NP.Earlier status note**Open**Classical UGC remains open. Hence this is precisely a counterexample to the ranked implication, with the left-module convention made explicit by the opposite algebra.
